page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance belonging to the DPLDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and a bundled 1229 GB local SSD. The processor architecture lacks AVX, AVX512, and AMX vector extensions but supports hardware-accelerated AES cryptography.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 57238.05 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12092.0. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1033.0 and a poor single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 6.99 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is solid, reaching 2231.84 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 143.96 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model yielding poor throughput under 4 tokens per second, though smaller 135M models achieve average generation speeds of 207.67 tokens per second.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D32plds_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-focused workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The inclusion of a 1229 GB local SSD provides high-capacity, low-latency storage, making it suitable for applications with high disk I/O requirements. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded application compiling, static web serving, Redis caching operations, and medium-scale database deployments that fit within the 64.0 GB memory limit.
description: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v5 is an ARM64 virtual machine powered by a 32-core Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 1229 GB of local SSD storage. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers dedicated CPU allocation without hyperthreading. Benchmarks show average multi-core capabilities, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 12092.0 and a static web serving throughput of 24.8 GB/sec, though single-core performance and large-model LLM inference are weak. Lacking AVX extensions but supporting AES cryptography, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-centric, low-memory tasks. It is best suited for multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, Redis caching, and database operations.
